_comment: The work the pacer runs when you're behind pace. Make these things you actually want — the value is the saved output file. Placeholders: {prompt} is filled from a task's prompt; output/prompt support {date} (2026-07-23), {datetime}, {id}, {outputDir}. cooldownMinutes stops a task re-running too often (e.g. 720 = twice a day at most).
_comment_chained: A task with "chain": true pursues a standing "mission" across many turns: each turn does a chunk of work AND writes the prompt for the next turn, carrying a "journal" of state forward. It runs confined to its own "workspace" directory with no network (build offline: code/content/plans, not deploys). Extra placeholders in a chained task: {turn} and {workDir}. Seeded from "seedPrompt"; stops at the model's done flag or "maxTurns". State lives in the agent's state.json under chains[id]; delete that entry to restart. A running {id}-journal.md is written alongside the output.

tasks.prompt: Give me a concise digest of notable developments this week in AI infrastructure and developer tooling. Group by theme, 5-8 bullets, each with why it matters in one line. Plain markdown.
Read the git log of the last 24 hours in ~/Desktop/Resource_Utilization_Dashboard and write a plain-language summary of what changed and why it matters, plus anything that looks risky or unfinished.

Here is a recurring problem I want to think through: {date}'s standing question is how to reduce context-switching during deep work. Give me three concrete experiments to try this week, with the tradeoffs of each.

tasks.mission: Create a project that will make me money with minimal ongoing work on my part. It must be buildable entirely offline inside your working directory (no deploys, accounts, or network) — e.g. a sellable code product/template, a digital info product, or reusable content — packaged so that I can take the finished folder to market with little effort.
tasks.seedPrompt: Turn 1: Pick ONE concrete, offline-buildable product idea that best fits the mission. In a few lines justify why it can earn with minimal upkeep. Then scaffold the project folder and write a README.md stating what it is, who buys it, how it makes money, and the build plan for the next few turns.
